name: Behind the Loop: Bringing The Invisible Labour Powering AI into Focus
description:

- ​A screening of Humans in the Loop, followed by a conversation with director Aranya Sahay

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: Murder in the Expanding Universe—Investigating Dark Energy & the Possible Death of the Cosmological Constant
description:
**About the event**

Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

The Universe is expanding, and one quantity, the cosmological constant, has been known to explain why the expansion is speeding up.... until now.

New data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) hints that the cosmological constant may not be constant after all.

Inspired by the film noir genre, this talk will address what we know about the Universe’s expansion so far, and whether the cosmological constant is dead for good. We will visit the crime scene, flash back through a century of clues, and question the witnesses: galaxies and quasars that each saw the universe at a different moment in time.

We will line up the suspects who may or may not have killed the cosmological constant, and cross-examine them with evidence that the Universe naturally provides us.

Here’s a case that is far from being open-and-shut.

**About the Speaker**

Dr. Basundhara Ghosh is a faculty of Physics at Azim Premji University, Bengaluru, and specialises in Theoretical Cosmology.

Prior to this, she was a DST-INSPIRE Faculty and a CV Raman Postdoctoral Fellow at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, and a DAAD Research Fellow at Heidelberg University, Germany.

She obtained her PhD from the University of Geneva, Switzerland and her MSc from the Indian Institute of Technology Bhubaneswar. Her research interests encompass the study of the Universe at late times, also known as the dark energy- dominated epoch.

When she is not studying the Universe or teaching in a classroom, she discusses films on her Instagram page @gangsofcinepur.

**Event Details**

📅 Saturday, 31 October

🕛 4 PM – 6 PM

📍 Atta Galatta, Indiranagar, Bengaluru

**Your ticket includes:**

• 1 complimentary kombucha from Umami Brew

• First-come, first-served seating

**About Pint of View**

Pint of View is India's Largest Lecture Community. We brought the lecture in bar format to India and are now expanding across the globe with chapters in 14 cities worldwide. Here, big ideas meet intimate spaces, and you walk in curious and walk out with a sharper lens on the world.

Book now and develop your own pint of view. 🍻

name: Signal Traces: Bengaluru by Thomas Lea Clarke
description:
Join us for the final presentation of Thomas Lea Clarke, bangaloREsident@Indian Music Experience Museum, before he heads back to Germany.

*Signal Traces: Bengaluru* is an exhibition by artist Thomas Lea Clarke, developed over two months spent listening to Bengaluru and discussing sound, music and memory with people whose lives and work engage with sound in different ways. Through interviews with musicians, artists, technicians, residents, instrument builders, a sound archaeologist and a neuroscientist, Clarke explores how sound lives on in recordings, voices, bodies, spaces and objects, and how different forms of listening can affect the experience of our environments.

The exhibition takes the form of a four-channel sound installation, a photographic series and a publication. In the sound installation, fragments of recorded conversations move through the space alongside field recordings and musical elements, forming a shifting listening environment in which personal recollection, everyday sound, musical practice and the material cultures of listening intersect. The photographic series focuses on the people, objects and spaces encountered during the project, tracing the physical environments and material forms through which sound is made, stored, repaired, transmitted and remembered. The publication presents the interviews in longer form, allowing conversations heard only fragmentarily within the installation to retain their individual context and complexity.

**Saturday, October 31**

**6:30pm onwards**

**Indian Music Experience Museum**

His live band expands this sound into a dynamic fusion of live percussion, Colombian flute, synthesizers, vocals and electronic production, bringing together traditional instrumentation and contemporary club music.

Joined by Guadalupe and Yulian, the live setup combines Colombian folk percussion and gaita with Akai-driven sequences, MPCs and synths, creating an immersive, rhythm-heavy performance rooted in Colombia while looking firmly toward the global dance floor.

Built across 12,000 sq. ft., the venue features a 600+ capacity performance space, world-class sound and lighting systems, and a diverse F&B proposition. name: Verse and Worse Karaoke with Aashish Paul
description:
**About the Event:**

Verse and Worse Karaoke with Aashish Paul - Dramatic duets, forgotten lyrics, guilty pleasure anthems - all welcome here. Hosted by Aashish Paul at The Humming Tree. No judgment, just good music and louder singalongs 😎

Join us this Tuesday!

**The Humming Tree:**

The Humming Tree - A grassroots performance venue in Bangalore, running from 2013 to 2019 and in the process becoming a cornerstone of Bangalore’s independent music, art, and cultural ecosystem.

Now, in 2026, The Humming Tree is back in a brand-new, purpose-designed space in Indiranagar. Built across 12,000 sq. ft., the venue features a 600+ capacity performance space, world-class sound and lighting systems, and a diverse F&B proposition. More than just a venue, it’s a hub for creativity, culture and collaboration.

name: An Hour of Stillness - An immersive sound experience
description:
Somewhere between the demands of the day and the things waiting for tomorrow, there is a little space to pause.

Join Sri for an immersive 60-minute sound experience with Himalayan singing bowls, crystal bowls, handpan, ocean drum and gong.

Through layers of sound, moments of quiet and a gentle return to the present, you'll have an hour to simply listen.

There's nothing to learn, no experience required and nothing you need to achieve.

Just come as you are. Get comfortable. Listen.

**What to expect**

- A gentle arrival and grounding
- An immersive journey through live instrumental sounds
- Moments of quiet and stillness
- Time to return slowly before the session closes

**Who is this for?**

Anyone looking to step away from the demands of everyday life and make a little room for themselves. No prior meditation or sound experience is needed.
